walkthroughs.body_html:
Quantities & Units in Mechanics — a core area of A-Level Maths.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Quantities & Units in Mechanics brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Quantities & Units in Mechanics.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: A particle starts from rest and accelerates at 4 m/s² for 3 seconds. Final velocity is:
options: 12 m/s
7 m/s

mcqs.q: Which SUVAT equation does NOT involve t?
options: v² = u² + 2as
v = u + at
s = ut + ½at²

mcqs.q: What is the reciprocal of the mixed number 2 1/3?
options: 3/7 — first convert to the improper fraction 7/3, then flip it.
Equal to 6, because 0.5 is half and so cancels out.
-2 1/3, because reciprocal means 'opposite'.
1/2 1/3, by flipping each part of the mixed number separately.
-7, because the negatives are being combined.
12 — the product of two negatives is positive.
-12, because there's a negative sign in the calculation.
-2 1/3, because reciprocal means 'opposite'.

mcqs.q: Is the result of 6 / 0.5 larger or smaller than 6?
options: Larger — dividing by a number less than 1 gives a bigger result (6 / 0.5 = 12).
Smaller, because division always makes numbers smaller.
Equal to 6, because 0.5 is half and so cancels out.
-2 1/3, because reciprocal means 'opposite'.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Displacement, velocity, acceleration”?
options: If a depends on t: v = ∫a dt; s = ∫v dt. Use calculus rather than SUVAT.
Speed is scalar (magnitude of velocity). Velocity is vector — has direction.
Take a = g = 9.8 m/s² downward (or 9.81). Use SUVAT for projectiles, free fall.
Displacement s (vector); velocity v = ds/dt; acceleration a = dv/dt = d²s/dt². All are vectors in 2D/3D.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Variable acceleration”?
options: If a depends on t: v = ∫a dt; s = ∫v dt. Use calculus rather than SUVAT.
Take a = g = 9.8 m/s² downward (or 9.81). Use SUVAT for projectiles, free fall.
Slope = acceleration; area under graph = displacement. Helpful for visualising motion.
Speed is scalar (magnitude of velocity). Velocity is vector — has direction.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “SUVAT equations”?
options: Speed is scalar (magnitude of velocity). Velocity is vector — has direction.
If a depends on t: v = ∫a dt; s = ∫v dt. Use calculus rather than SUVAT.
Displacement s (vector); velocity v = ds/dt; acceleration a = dv/dt = d²s/dt². All are vectors in 2D/3D.
For constant acceleration: v = u + at; s = ut + ½at²; v² = u² + 2as; s = ((u+v)/2)t. Useful when a is constant.

Displacement s (vector); velocity v = ds/dt; acceleration a = dv/dt = d²s/dt². All are vectors in 2D/3D.
Slope = acceleration; area under graph = displacement. Helpful for visualising motion.
